description:
pkix-ct/src/sct.rs:137-138

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct SctList(pub Vec<SignedCertificateTimestamp>);
```

PKIX-ppbr.8 already filed this from the "callers can bypass parser
invariants" angle. The API-contract / defensive-forcing angle:

`SctList::from_extension_value` and `from_serialized_list` are the
"validated" paths — they enforce RFC 6962 §3.3's
`sct_list<1..2^16-1>` constraint (no empty list) and per-SCT
parsing constraints (version=0, well-formed wire layout).

`SctList(vec![])` is the "trust-me" path — callers can build any
list, including an empty one. The verifier's
`verify_embedded_scts` path (lines 400-404) re-checks `is_empty()`
and returns `Error::NoScts` for an empty list. But every other
caller that walks `SctList::0` directly skips that check.

Real callers (e.g., `pkix-chain::verify_one`) iterate over
`sct_list.0` and verify each. An empty list means "zero
verifications, threshold not met". Some callers may not check
length and may silently treat empty as "no SCTs to verify, pass".

Recommendation:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct SctList(Vec<SignedCertificateTimestamp>);

impl SctList {
    pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[SignedCertificateTimestamp] { &self.0 }
    pub fn into_inner(self) -> Vec<SignedCertificateTimestamp> { self.0 }
}

impl std::ops::Deref for SctList {
    type Target = [SignedCertificateTimestamp];
    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target { &self.0 }
}

impl IntoIterator for SctList { ... }
```

Now construction is only through the parsers; iteration and slice
access work via `Deref`. The tuple-field becomes private and the
invariants from the parser are preserved.

Cost: existing callers using `&sct_list.0` need to switch to
`&sct_list[..]` or `sct_list.as_slice()` — but the `Deref` impl
makes this trivial. PKIX-ppbr.8 should land this fix.

Priority P2 because:
- defensive-forcing: callers must re-check invariants
- immutability: the `pub` field is locked once shipped
- both already-filed PKIX-ppbr.8 carries the bug angle.

This issue is filed under defensive-forcing to keep the per-section
counts honest; the actual fix should converge on PKIX-ppbr.8.
title: SctList(pub Vec<...>) tuple-struct admits construction with invalid SCTs — every caller validates
